final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence; the response mostly narrowed and clarified the claim using the same record and expressly conceded the key gap. That narrowing is useful, but it does not satisfy the policy predicate. The governing policy allows certification only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. The admissible evidence supports aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, but it also establishes a current material subgroup regression, a stale prior approval, and only an informal monitoring comment without reviewed mitigation or disclosure text. Because there is still no admissible proof that the current model card or release documentation has been updated for this release, the strongest supported conclusion remains that certification is not yet supported on the present record. This is not merely a caveated-compliance case: the caveat identifies an unresolved compliance condition that has not been evidenced as satisfied.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation or model card has actually been updated to reflect the current evaluation results for this release.
The telecom outage-credits slice is 1.1 percentage points below the warning threshold for a named launch use case, so the limitation is material under the policy.
No admissible reviewed disclosure language, approved mitigation, or approved risk acceptance is attached to this release.
The prior approval is stale because it predates the current retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch.
The release-thread monitoring comment is contextual only and does not satisfy the policy requirement for current evidence or reviewed mitigation.
